topicName: Native UI Components vs Web Views
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Native UI Components vs Web Views in NativeScript"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"When building cross-platform mobile applications with NativeScript, one of the most fundamental architectural decisions you will make is choosing between truly native UI components and Web Views. Understanding the performance, UX, and development trade-offs is crucial for the success of your app."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"What are Native UI Components?"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"NativeScript maps its UI modules directly to the underlying platform's native UI elements. A <Button> in NativeScript compiles into a native Android Button (android.widget.Button) and a native iOS button (UIButton). There is no abstraction layer like a web browser rendering DOM elements."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Direct access to native APIs and hardware acceleration."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Platform-specific look, feel, and gesture handling out of the box."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Optimal performance for animations, scrolling, and heavy data rendering."},{"order":8,"type":"heading","text":"What are Web Views?"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Web Views embed a mini-browser inside your native application using components like WebView on Android and WKWebView on iOS. This allows you to render HTML, CSS, and JavaScript directly inside your native shell, similar to how frameworks like Cordova or Ionic operate."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Ideal for displaying rich text, marketing pages, or complex documentation."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Allows seamless reuse of existing web applications and components."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Heavier memory footprint and potential performance bottlenecks during heavy animations."},{"order":13,"type":"heading","text":"Code Implementation Example"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Below is an example showing how to declare both a Native UI component and a WebView side-by-side in a NativeScript XML layout."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"<Page xmlns="http://schemas.nativescript.org/tns.xsd">
  <StackLayout class="p-20">
    <!-- Native UI Component -->
    <Button text="Click Native" class="btn btn-primary" tap="onTap" />
    
    <!-- Web View Component -->
    <WebView src="https://nativescript.org" height="300" />
  </StackLayout>
</Page>"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"When to Choose Which?"},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use Native UI Components for core navigation, lists, forms, and performance-critical interactions."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use Web Views when integrating third-party web content, payment gateways, or building hybrid features where web technologies are mandatory."}]
